premises.text: People spend excessive time managing their email inboxes instead of focusing on priorities.
premises.evidence_span: 900 million people spend 20 hours a week acting as if their job is to process their inbox.

premises.text: Capturing all priorities in one place is necessary for making good decisions.
premises.evidence_span: you have to get them all in one place to make good decisions.

premises.text: Triage is essential for making decisions on every item in the inbox.
premises.evidence_span: Triage is making decisions on every item when you see it.

premises.text: Planning is necessary to make wise decisions about how to use time effectively.
premises.evidence_span: you have to make wise decisions with it, because it will be gone.

premises.text: Completing important tasks is crucial for productivity.
premises.evidence_span: actually do the work that you think is most important until it is complete.

premises.text: Handle is a unique tool designed to manage priorities effectively.
premises.evidence_span: we built the whole thing, introducing the world's first priority engine, Handle.

premises.text: The Handlebar feature allows for quick triage of emails and tasks.
premises.evidence_span: The Handlebar is even faster, it uses the keyboard, and can move as fast as you can think.

premises.text: Users can manage their tasks and emails efficiently with Handle.
premises.evidence_span: My inbox is at zero. Now I can focus on some real work.

premises.text: Handle helps users maintain focus on their key deliverables without context switching.
premises.evidence_span: I can jump in and be productive immediately. No context switching.

premises.text: Handle aims to improve users' overall life balance by managing priorities.
premises.evidence_span: The disruption is going home and having dinner with your family without checking your iPhone.

value.text: Users can achieve better productivity and work-life balance through effective priority management.
value.evidence_span: Handle is not about handle. It's about you and doing what you feel is most important.

notes: No external knowledge or traction metrics included.
